LESSON: TRANSPORT IN PLANTS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GENERAL SCIENCE
Strand: Life Science 1.3 Nutrition in Animals (10 lessons) ● Chemical and Mechanical dig
Topic 1.4: Transport in plants
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Transport in plants, part of Life Science 1.3 Nutrition in Animals (10 lessons) ● Chemical and Mechanical dig in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 GENERAL SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: Why is transport in plants important? 2. How do plants absorb water and mineral salts?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Transport in plants together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Citizenship: as the learner sensitises the community on the importance of watering and manuring plants to sustain plant

growth.

● Learning to learn: as the learner reflects on experiments on factors affecting transpiration in plants.

Values:
● Unity: as the learner engages in assigned roles while harmoniously working with others while conducting an experiment

to investigate factors affecting transpiration.

● Patriotism: as the learner sensitises the community on the importance of watering and manuring plants to sustain plant

growth.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

● Socio Economic and environmental issues - Safety and security: as the learner observes safety precautions as they carry

out experiments in groups to investigate factors affecting transpiration in plants.

● Socio Economic and environmental issues - Environmental conservation: as the learner creates awareness in the

community on the use of fertilisers (Di-ammonium phosphate, Calcium Ammonium Nitrate, Urea) in boosting crop

production.

Suggested Learning Resources:

• Posters in print and braille

• Print textbooks in appropriate font and colour,

• Braille textbooks,

• Digital devices with assistive technology such as screen readers and screen magnifiers,

• Tactile diagrams of plant specimens.
